"""Independent behavioral probe for the PEP 752 task (second reward channel).

Usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>

Writes ``{"passed": bool, "failed": [...], "checks": N}``. ``passed`` is true
only when every check below holds. Any unexpected error fails closed
(``passed`` is false, never missing).

WHY THIS EXISTS

The graded suite's verdicts travel through the JUnit XML report, which is
written inside the same container -- and the same process -- as agent code:
the agent-owned interpreter runs the regrtest process, and the agent's own
package is imported into it. In-process code can therefore rewrite the
report after a genuine failing run (an atexit hook suffices) and a
report-only grader scores reward 1. This probe closes that route: it
re-checks the specified behaviors directly -- including negative cases --
and NEVER reads the JUnit report. The reward requires this probe AND every
required suite id, so a forged report alone can no longer score.

WHY THREE PROCESSES

An earlier single-process probe imported the submitted package in the same
process that wrote its verdict file, so a shutdown hook inside the package
could overwrite the genuine payload afterwards and the reward accepted the
forgery. Splitting off a verdict-writing parent closed that route but not
the next one: the child still imports agent code to run the checks, and
that code can patch the test framework (``unittest.TestCase.run``) or arm
a ``sys.settrace`` hook that swaps the check functions for no-ops, forging
a passing payload the parent would then faithfully write. A parent that
merely writes what the child computed authenticates nothing.

This probe therefore splits in three. The CHECK CHILD runs in a fresh
locked-down interpreter (absolute repo path, ``-I -S``, neutral cwd,
scrubbed environment, script from the verifier-owned ``/tests`` tree),
imports the implementation under test, runs every check, and prints its
verdict as one marked line on stdout. The ATTEST GRANDCHILD runs the same
locked-down way but NEVER imports agent code: it only hashes the check
functions' bytecode, giving the parent ground truth no submission can
influence. The PARENT never imports agent-controlled code -- it spawns
both, demands exactly one well-formed result line on a zero exit from
each, requires the child's per-check code hashes to equal the
grandchild's (a swapped check has different bytecode, however its
filename was faked), and only then writes the verdict file, after both
(and any hook the child armed) are dead. Anything the child writes to
the verdict path is moot: the parent overwrites it last. Every anomaly
-- crash, timeout, missing or doubled result line, malformed payload,
attestation mismatch -- fails closed.

The probe pins specified behavior only (the same contract the graded suite
is authored from), never reference-implementation internals, so any correct
alternate implementation passes it.
"""

"""Independent behavioral probe for the PEP 752 task (second reward channel).

Usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>

Writes ``{"passed": bool, "failed": [...], "checks": N}``. ``passed`` is true
only when every check below holds. Any unexpected error fails closed
(``passed`` is false, never missing).

WHY THIS EXISTS

The graded suite's verdicts travel through the JUnit XML report, which is
written inside the same container -- and the same process -- as agent code:
the agent-owned interpreter runs the regrtest process, and the agent's own
package is imported into it. In-process code can therefore rewrite the
report after a genuine failing run (an atexit hook suffices) and a
report-only grader scores reward 1. This probe closes that route: it
re-checks the specified behaviors directly -- including negative cases --
and NEVER reads the JUnit report. The reward requires this probe AND every
required suite id, so a forged report alone can no longer score.

WHY THREE PROCESSES

An earlier single-process probe imported the submitted package in the same
process that wrote its verdict file, so a shutdown hook inside the package
could overwrite the genuine payload afterwards and the reward accepted the
forgery. Splitting off a verdict-writing parent closed that route but not
the next one: the child still imports agent code to run the checks, and
that code can patch the test framework (``unittest.TestCase.run``) or arm
a ``sys.settrace`` hook that swaps the check functions for no-ops, forging
a passing payload the parent would then faithfully write. A parent that
merely writes what the child computed authenticates nothing.

This probe therefore splits in three. The CHECK CHILD runs in a fresh
locked-down interpreter (absolute repo path, ``-I -S``, neutral cwd,
scrubbed environment, script from the verifier-owned ``/tests`` tree),
imports the implementation under test, runs every check, and prints its
verdict as one marked line on stdout. The ATTEST GRANDCHILD runs the same
locked-down way but NEVER imports agent code: it only hashes the check
functions' bytecode, giving the parent ground truth no submission can
influence. The PARENT never imports agent-controlled code -- it spawns
both, demands exactly one well-formed result line on a zero exit from
each, requires the child's per-check code hashes to equal the
grandchild's (a swapped check has different bytecode, however its
filename was faked), and only then writes the verdict file, after both
(and any hook the child armed) are dead. Anything the child writes to
the verdict path is moot: the parent overwrites it last. Every anomaly
-- crash, timeout, missing or doubled result line, malformed payload,
attestation mismatch -- fails closed.

The probe pins specified behavior only (the same contract the graded suite
is authored from), never reference-implementation internals, so any correct
alternate implementation passes it.
"""

def _code_hash(func):

    return hashlib.sha256(func.__code__.co_code).hexdigest()

"""Generate and verify offline fixtures for the package namespace examples."""

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys


def _package():
    # Also support an installed host Python without adding the checkout's
    # entire standard library (which may require a newer interpreter).
    source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'Lib' / 'packagenamespaces'
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        'packagenamespaces', source / '__init__.py',
        submodule_search_locations=[str(source)],
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[spec.name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def generate(directory):
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fixtures = {
        'grants.json': {'grants': [
            {'name': 'acme', 'owner': 'Acme'},
            {'name': 'acme-tools', 'owner': 'Acme'},
        ]},
        'projects.json': {'projects': {
            'acme-tools-cli': 'Acme', 'acme-legacy': 'Other',
            'unreserved': 'Other',
        }},
        'grandfathered.json': {'grandfathered': ['acme-legacy']},
        'second-index.json': {
            'grants': [], 'projects': {'acme-tools-cli': 'Acme'},
        },
    }
    for name, value in fixtures.items():
        (directory / name).write_text(
            json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n',
            encoding='utf-8',
        )


def _require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def _validate_grants(value, package):
    _require(isinstance(value, list), 'grants must be an array')
    for grant in value:
        _require(isinstance(grant, dict)
                 and set(grant) == {'name', 'owner'}, 'invalid grant entry')
        package.Grant(grant['name'], grant['owner'])


def _validate_projects(value, package):
    _require(isinstance(value, dict) and value,
             'projects must be a non-empty object')
    for name, owner in value.items():
        package.Grant(name, owner)


def verify(directory):
    package = _package()
    data = {}
    for filename, keys in (
        ('grants.json', {'grants'}),
        ('projects.json', {'projects'}),
        ('grandfathered.json', {'grandfathered'}),
        ('second-index.json', {'grants', 'projects'}),
    ):
        value = json.loads((directory / filename).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        _require(isinstance(value, dict) and set(value) == keys,
                 f'invalid {filename} schema')
        data[filename] = value

    # Validate every fixture's structure and entry types before any behavioral
    # checks, including the independent repository's data.
    grants = data['grants.json']['grants']
    _validate_grants(grants, package)
    _require(len(grants) >= 2, 'at least two grants are required')
    projects = data['projects.json']['projects']
    _validate_projects(projects, package)
    exempt = data['grandfathered.json']['grandfathered']
    _require(isinstance(exempt, list), 'grandfathered must be an array')
    for project in exempt:
        _require(package.is_valid_namespace(project), 'invalid exempt project')
    second = data['second-index.json']
    _validate_grants(second['grants'], package)
    _require(second['grants'] == [], 'second index must have no grants')
    _validate_projects(second['projects'], package)

    index = package.RepositoryIndex()
    for grant in grants:
        index.store.reserve(grant['name'], grant['owner'])
    for project, owner in projects.items():
        index.register_project(project, owner)
    for project in exempt:
        index.grandfathered.add(project)
    other = package.RepositoryIndex()
    for project, owner in second['projects'].items():
        other.register_project(project, owner)

    policy = package.SecurityPolicy(['acme', 'acme-tools'], 'Acme')
    _require(index.store.namespaces() == ['acme', 'acme-tools'],
             'unexpected example grants')
    _require(index.store.parent('acme-tools') == 'acme', 'missing parent')
    _require(index.store.children('acme') == ['acme-tools'], 'missing child')
    _require(policy.allows('acme-tools-cli', index), 'owned project denied')
    _require(not policy.allows('acme-legacy', index),
             'foreign project allowed')
    _require(not policy.allows('acme-tools-cli', other),
             'grant leaked across repositories')
    _require(other.project_owner('acme-tools-cli') == 'Acme',
             'second index must register the owned project')
    for project in index.projects():
        package.authorize_upload(project, index.project_owner(project),
                                 index.store, index.grandfathered)
    try:
        package.authorize_upload('acme-new', 'Other', index.store)
    except package.UploadConflictError as error:
        _require(error.status_code == 409 and error.owner == 'Other',
                 'invalid upload conflict details')
    else:
        raise ValueError('foreign upload was allowed')
    index.store.remove('acme-tools')
    index.store.remove('acme')
    _require(index.project_detail('acme-tools-cli')['namespaces'] is None,
             'removed grants still appear in metadata')
    print('verify: all checks passed')


def main():
    try:
        command, directory = sys.argv[1:]
        if command == 'generate':
            generate(Path(directory))
        elif command == 'verify':
            verify(Path(directory))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown command: {command}')
    except Exception as error:
        print(f'error: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Generate and verify offline fixtures for the package namespace examples."""

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys


def _package():
    # Also support an installed host Python without adding the checkout's
    # entire standard library (which may require a newer interpreter).
    source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / 'Lib' / 'packagenamespaces'
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        'packagenamespaces', source / '__init__.py',
        submodule_search_locations=[str(source)],
    )
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[spec.name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def generate(directory):
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fixtures = {
        'grants.json': {'grants': [
            {'name': 'acme', 'owner': 'Acme'},
            {'name': 'acme-tools', 'owner': 'Acme'},
        ]},
        'projects.json': {'projects': {
            'acme-tools-cli': 'Acme', 'acme-legacy': 'Other',
            'unreserved': 'Other',
        }},
        'grandfathered.json': {'grandfathered': ['acme-legacy']},
        'second-index.json': {
            'grants': [], 'projects': {'acme-tools-cli': 'Acme'},
        },
    }
    for name, value in fixtures.items():
        (directory / name).write_text(
            json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + '\n',
            encoding='utf-8',
        )


def _require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def _validate_grants(value, package):
    _require(isinstance(value, list), 'grants must be an array')
    for grant in value:
        _require(isinstance(grant, dict)
                 and set(grant) == {'name', 'owner'}, 'invalid grant entry')
        package.Grant(grant['name'], grant['owner'])


def _validate_projects(value, package):
    _require(isinstance(value, dict) and value,
             'projects must be a non-empty object')
    for name, owner in value.items():
        package.Grant(name, owner)


def verify(directory):
    package = _package()
    data = {}
    for filename, keys in (
        ('grants.json', {'grants'}),
        ('projects.json', {'projects'}),
        ('grandfathered.json', {'grandfathered'}),
        ('second-index.json', {'grants', 'projects'}),
    ):
        value = json.loads((directory / filename).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
        _require(isinstance(value, dict) and set(value) == keys,
                 f'invalid {filename} schema')
        data[filename] = value

    # Validate every fixture's structure and entry types before any behavioral
    # checks, including the independent repository's data.
    grants = data['grants.json']['grants']
    _validate_grants(grants, package)
    _require(len(grants) >= 2, 'at least two grants are required')
    projects = data['projects.json']['projects']
    _validate_projects(projects, package)
    exempt = data['grandfathered.json']['grandfathered']
    _require(isinstance(exempt, list), 'grandfathered must be an array')
    for project in exempt:
        _require(package.is_valid_namespace(project), 'invalid exempt project')
    second = data['second-index.json']
    _validate_grants(second['grants'], package)
    _require(second['grants'] == [], 'second index must have no grants')
    _validate_projects(second['projects'], package)

    index = package.RepositoryIndex()
    for grant in grants:
        index.store.reserve(grant['name'], grant['owner'])
    for project, owner in projects.items():
        index.register_project(project, owner)
    for project in exempt:
        index.grandfathered.add(project)
    other = package.RepositoryIndex()
    for project, owner in second['projects'].items():
        other.register_project(project, owner)

    policy = package.SecurityPolicy(['acme', 'acme-tools'], 'Acme')
    _require(index.store.namespaces() == ['acme', 'acme-tools'],
             'unexpected example grants')
    _require(index.store.parent('acme-tools') == 'acme', 'missing parent')
    _require(index.store.children('acme') == ['acme-tools'], 'missing child')
    _require(policy.allows('acme-tools-cli', index), 'owned project denied')
    _require(not policy.allows('acme-legacy', index),
             'foreign project allowed')
    _require(not policy.allows('acme-tools-cli', other),
             'grant leaked across repositories')
    _require(other.project_owner('acme-tools-cli') == 'Acme',
             'second index must register the owned project')
    for project in index.projects():
        package.authorize_upload(project, index.project_owner(project),
                                 index.store, index.grandfathered)
    try:
        package.authorize_upload('acme-new', 'Other', index.store)
    except package.UploadConflictError as error:
        _require(error.status_code == 409 and error.owner == 'Other',
                 'invalid upload conflict details')
    else:
        raise ValueError('foreign upload was allowed')
    index.store.remove('acme-tools')
    index.store.remove('acme')
    _require(index.project_detail('acme-tools-cli')['namespaces'] is None,
             'removed grants still appear in metadata')
    print('verify: all checks passed')


def main():
    try:
        command, directory = sys.argv[1:]
        if command == 'generate':
            generate(Path(directory))
        elif command == 'verify':
            verify(Path(directory))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown command: {command}')
    except Exception as error:
        print(f'error: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

def harness_scripts_use_no_network():
    # Behavioral, never textual: no word in either script is matched, so a
    # comment merely mentioning a network tool passes. Instead the scripts
    # run with every network command shadowed by a stub that logs its
    # invocation and fails: genuine shell-outs to the network then fail
    # (the stub's exit 1 under `set -e`, or the empty-log assertion),
    # while offline scripts succeed with zero invocations. Commented
    # copies prove the point directly by still passing.
    network_cmds = ("curl", "wget", "ssh", "scp", "sftp", "ftp", "lftp",
                    "telnet", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "httpx")
    comment = ("# offline by design: curl wget ssh scp sftp ftp lftp "
               "telnet nc ncat socat httpx urllib http.client\n")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        stubdir = os.path.join(tmp, "stubs")
        os.mkdir(stubdir)
        log = os.path.join(tmp, "invocations.log")
        for cmd in network_cmds:
            stub = os.path.join(stubdir, cmd)
            with open(stub, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(f"#!/bin/bash\necho {cmd} >> {log}\nexit 1\n")
            os.chmod(stub, 0o755)
        env = {"PATH": stubdir + os.pathsep + "/usr/bin:/bin",
               "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"}
        fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("gen_fixtures.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("verify_offline.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()
        # Copies carrying network-word comments behave identically. The
        # copies sit in a mirrored Tools/ layout with Lib linked back to
        # the repo, because the verifier derives its root from its own
        # path; only the trailing comment differs from the real scripts.
        mirror = os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Tools", "packagenamespaces")
        os.makedirs(mirror)
        os.symlink(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "Lib"),
                   os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Lib"))
        commented = {}
        for script in ("gen_fixtures.sh", "verify_offline.sh"):
            with open(_tools_path(script), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                content = handle.read()
            copy_path = os.path.join(mirror, script)
            with open(copy_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(content + comment)
            commented[script] = copy_path
        alt_fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "alt-fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["gen_fixtures.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["verify_offline.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()

def _parent_main(argv):
    """Spawn the child, validate its one result line, write the verdict.

    This process never imports agent-controlled code. The verdict file is
    written only here, after the child has exited, so a shutdown hook the
    child armed cannot rewrite it afterwards: anything it wrote is moot.
    A second spawn -- the attestation grandchild, which never imports
    agent code either -- supplies ground-truth check hashes the child's
    per-check digests must equal, so swapped checks fail closed even
    when the child's own verdict claims they passed.
    """
    if len(argv) != 3:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: probe.py <repo-root> <output-json>\n")
        return 2
    repo_root, output_path = argv[1], argv[2]

    def fail_closed(reason):
        payload = {"passed": False, "failed": [reason],
                   "checks": len(CHECKS)}
        try:
            with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
                handle.write("\n")
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
            return 2
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {reason}\n")
        return 0

    def spawn(mode):
        """Run one locked-down grandchild, return its marked payload."""
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                [child_bin, "-I", "-S",
                 os.path.abspath(__file__), mode, repo_root],
                capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=900,
                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True,
                env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"},
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process timed out"
        except Exception as exc:  # Missing binary, decode failure, ...
            return None, f"probe: cannot run {mode} process: {exc!r}"
        if proc.stderr:
            sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} process exited {proc.returncode}"
        lines = [line for line in proc.stdout.splitlines()
                 if line.startswith(MARKER)]
        if len(lines) != 1:
            return None, (f"probe: {mode} expected 1 result line, "
                          f"saw {len(lines)}")
        try:
            return json.loads(lines[0][len(MARKER):]), None
        except ValueError as exc:
            return None, f"probe: {mode} result line is not JSON: {exc}"

    child_bin = os.path.join(repo_root, "python")
    try:
        with open(child_bin, "rb") as handle:
            magic = handle.read(4)
    except OSError as exc:
        return fail_closed(f"probe: cannot read check interpreter: {exc!r}")
    # Never execute a replacement: only a built ELF executable may run the
    # checks (run_script.sh already relinked a non-ELF binary; anything
    # still wrong here fails closed instead of running it).
    if magic != b"\x7fELF" or not os.access(child_bin, os.X_OK):
        return fail_closed(
            "probe: check interpreter is not a built executable")
    payload, error = spawn("--child")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    if (not isinstance(payload, dict)
            or payload.get("checks") != len(CHECKS)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("passed"), bool)
            or not isinstance(payload.get("failed"), list)
            or not all(isinstance(entry, str)
                       for entry in payload["failed"])
            or not isinstance(payload.get("attest"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: result line has a bad shape")
    attested, error = spawn("--attest")
    if error is not None:
        return fail_closed(error)
    expected_names = [name for name, _ in CHECKS]
    if (not isinstance(attested, dict)
            or attested.get("names") != expected_names
            or not isinstance(attested.get("hashes"), dict)):
        return fail_closed("probe: attestation has a bad shape")
    truth = attested["hashes"]
    claimed = payload["attest"]
    for side in ("pre", "post"):
        digests = claimed.get(side)
        if not isinstance(digests, dict):
            return fail_closed(
                f"probe: attestation {side} has a bad shape")
        for name in expected_names:
            if digests.get(name) != truth.get(name):
                return fail_closed(
                    f"probe: check code mismatch for {name} ({side})")
    try:
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            handle.write("\n")
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: cannot write {output_path}: {exc}\n")
        return 2
    if payload["passed"]:
        sys.stderr.write(f"probe: all {len(CHECKS)} checks passed\n")
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(
            f"probe: {len(payload['failed'])}/{len(CHECKS)} checks failed\n")
        for failure in sorted(payload["failed"]):
            sys.stderr.write(f"probe: FAIL {failure}\n")
    return 0

"""Parse the runner-written JUnit XML report into the MSL verdict shape.

Usage: parser.py <stdout-file> <stderr-file> <output-json>

The console streams exist for logs only and are NEVER grading input: agent
code running inside the suite can print arbitrary text, so verdicts come
exclusively from the XML file regrtest itself wrote at the end of a genuine
run (``--junit-xml``). A run that never got there -- crashed, ``os._exit``'d
out of ``sitecustomize``, killed -- leaves no report and grades zero tests.

Writes::

    {"tests": [{"name": "<dotted id>", "status": "PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR"}]}

The dotted id is the testcase ``name`` attribute (``test.id()``), identical
to the id the console channel used to emit. When one id appears more than
once (regrtest reruns) the worst status wins, so a later pass can never
mask a real failure.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

JUNIT_XML = os.environ.get("LAMBO_JUNIT_XML", "/tmp/lambo-junit.xml")

# Worst first: a later pass never outranks a real failure.
SEVERITY = {"ERROR": 4, "FAILED": 3, "PASSED": 2, "SKIPPED": 1}

VALID = frozenset(SEVERITY)


def classify(case):
    """Map a JUnit testcase element to an MSL status."""
    for child in case:
        tag = child.tag
        if tag == "error":
            return "ERROR"
        if tag == "failure":
            return "FAILED"
        if tag == "skipped":
            return "SKIPPED"
        if tag == "output":
            # Expected failure: ran, failed as anticipated. Counts as
            # skipped, matching the old console channel's mapping.
            return "SKIPPED"
        if tag == "outcome" and (child.text or "").strip() == "UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS":
            return "FAILED"
    return "PASSED"


def parse_report(path, verdicts):
    """Fold testcase verdicts from one JUnit file into the verdict map."""
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        sys.stderr.write(f"parser: no JUnit report at {path} (run crashed?)\n")
        return
    except ET.ParseError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"parser: cannot parse {path}: {exc}\n")
        return
    except OSError as exc:
        sys.stderr.write(f"parser: cannot read {path}: {exc}\n")
        return
    for case in root.iter("testcase"):
        name = case.get("name")
        if not name:
            continue
        status = classify(case)
        current = verdicts.get(name)
        if current is None or SEVERITY[status] > SEVERITY[current]:
            verdicts[name] = status


def validate_contract(payload):
    """Exit non-zero unless the payload is the exact MSL shape."""
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("parser: output is not a JSON object\n")
        return False
    tests = payload.get("tests")
    if not isinstance(tests, list):
        sys.stderr.write("parser: output has no `tests` list\n")
        return False
    seen = set()
    for entry in tests:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            sys.stderr.write("parser: test entry is not an object\n")
            return False
        name = entry.get("name")
        status = entry.get("status")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            sys.stderr.write("parser: test entry has a bad name\n")
            return False
        if status not in VALID:
            sys.stderr.write(f"parser: status {status!r} for {name} is invalid\n")
            return False
        if name in seen:
            sys.stderr.write(f"parser: duplicate verdict for {name}\n")
            return False
        seen.add(name)
    return True


def main(argv):
    if len(argv) != 4:
        sys.stderr.write("usage: parser.py <stdout> <stderr> <output-json>\n")
        return 2
    output_path = argv[3]

    # comment merely mentioning a network tool passes. Instead the scripts
    # run with every network command shadowed by a stub that logs its
    # invocation and fails: genuine shell-outs to the network then fail
    # (the stub's exit 1 under `set -e`, or the empty-log assertion),
    # while offline scripts succeed with zero invocations. Commented
    # copies prove the point directly by still passing.

                    "telnet", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "httpx")

               "telnet nc ncat socat httpx urllib http.client\n")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        stubdir = os.path.join(tmp, "stubs")
        os.mkdir(stubdir)

            stub = os.path.join(stubdir, cmd)
            with open(stub, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(f"#!/bin/bash\necho {cmd} >> {log}\nexit 1\n")

            ["bash", _tools_path("gen_fixtures.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr

            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()
        # Copies carrying network-word comments behave identically. The
        # copies sit in a mirrored Tools/ layout with Lib linked back to
        # the repo, because the verifier derives its root from its own
        # path; only the trailing comment differs from the real scripts.
        mirror = os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Tools", "packagenamespaces")
        os.makedirs(mirror)
        os.symlink(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "Lib"),
                   os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Lib"))
        commented = {}
        for script in ("gen_fixtures.sh", "verify_offline.sh"):
            with open(_tools_path(script), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                content = handle.read()

            with open(copy_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:

        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["verify_offline.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()

"""Installer policies requiring repository-local namespace ownership."""

from .grants import InvalidNamespaceError, _validate_name, _validate_owner
from .matching import namespace_matches
from .normalize import normalize_name

__all__ = ['SecurityPolicy']


class SecurityPolicy:
    """Allow projects owned by owner under its active policy namespaces."""

    def __init__(self, namespaces, owner):
        _validate_owner(owner)
        if isinstance(namespaces, str):
            namespaces = (namespaces,)
        try:
            namespaces = iter(namespaces)
        except TypeError:
            raise InvalidNamespaceError(
                'namespaces must be an iterable of names'
            ) from None
        self._namespaces = tuple(_validate_name(name) for name in namespaces)
        self._owner = owner

    @property
    def namespaces(self):
        return self._namespaces

    @property
    def owner(self):
        return self._owner

    def allows(self, project, index):
        """Check project ownership and an active grant on this index."""
        project = normalize_name(project)
        if (not index.supports_namespaces
                or index.project_owner(project) != self.owner):
            return False
        for namespace in self.namespaces:
            grant = index.store.get(namespace)
            if (grant is not None and grant.owner == self.owner
                    and namespace_matches(namespace, project)):
                return True
        return False

    def evaluate(self, requirements, index):
        """Return normalized project names mapped to their policy decisions."""
        return {normalize_name(project): self.allows(project, index)
                for project in requirements}
"""Upload authorization and exemptions for pre-existing projects."""

from .grants import _validate_name, _validate_owner
from .normalize import normalize_name

__all__ = [
    'CONFLICT_STATUS', 'UploadConflictError', 'GrandfatheredRegistry',
    'authorize_upload',
]

CONFLICT_STATUS = 409


class UploadConflictError(Exception):
    """An uploader does not own a matching reserved namespace."""

    status_code = CONFLICT_STATUS

    def __init__(self, project, namespace, owner):
        self.project = normalize_name(project)
        self.namespace = normalize_name(namespace)
        self.owner = owner
        super().__init__(
            f'409 Conflict: {owner!r} cannot upload {self.project!r}; '
            f'namespace {self.namespace!r} is reserved'
        )


class GrandfatheredRegistry:
    """Keep normalized project names exempt from namespace upload checks."""

    def __init__(self, projects=()):
        self._projects = set()
        for project in projects:
            self.add(project)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._projects)

    def __contains__(self, project):
        return (isinstance(project, str)
                and normalize_name(project) in self._projects)

    def add(self, project):
        """Exempt a project from namespace upload checks."""
        self._projects.add(_validate_name(project))

    def discard(self, project):
        """Remove an exemption, if present."""
        self._projects.discard(normalize_name(project))

    def covers(self, project):
        """Return whether the normalized project is exempt."""
        return project in self

    def projects(self):
        """Return exempt project names in sorted order."""
        return sorted(self._projects)


def authorize_upload(project, owner, store, grandfathered=None):
    """Return True when allowed, otherwise raise UploadConflictError.

    Validate the uploader before consulting grants, even for unreserved or
    grandfathered projects.  Exemptions apply to complete project names.
    """
    _validate_owner(owner)
    project = _validate_name(project)
    if grandfathered is not None and grandfathered.covers(project):
        return True
    for grant in store.matching(project):
        if grant.owner != owner:
            raise UploadConflictError(project, grant.name, owner)
    return True

def validate_contract(payload):
    """Exit non-zero unless the payload is the exact MSL shape."""
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("parser: output is not a JSON object\n")
        return False
    tests = payload.get("tests")
    if not isinstance(tests, list):
        sys.stderr.write("parser: output has no `tests` list\n")
        return False
    seen = set()
    for entry in tests:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            sys.stderr.write("parser: test entry is not an object\n")
            return False
        name = entry.get("name")
        status = entry.get("status")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            sys.stderr.write("parser: test entry has a bad name\n")
            return False
        if status not in VALID:
            sys.stderr.write(f"parser: status {status!r} for {name} is invalid\n")
            return False
        if name in seen:
            sys.stderr.write(f"parser: duplicate verdict for {name}\n")
            return False

def harness_scripts_use_no_network():
    # Behavioral, never textual: no word in either script is matched, so a
    # comment merely mentioning a network tool passes. Instead the scripts
    # run with every network command shadowed by a stub that logs its
    # invocation and fails: genuine shell-outs to the network then fail
    # (the stub's exit 1 under `set -e`, or the empty-log assertion),
    # while offline scripts succeed with zero invocations. Commented
    # copies prove the point directly by still passing.
    network_cmds = ("curl", "wget", "ssh", "scp", "sftp", "ftp", "lftp",
                    "telnet", "nc", "ncat", "socat", "httpx")
    comment = ("# offline by design: curl wget ssh scp sftp ftp lftp "
               "telnet nc ncat socat httpx urllib http.client\n")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        stubdir = os.path.join(tmp, "stubs")
        os.mkdir(stubdir)
        log = os.path.join(tmp, "invocations.log")
        for cmd in network_cmds:
            stub = os.path.join(stubdir, cmd)
            with open(stub, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(f"#!/bin/bash\necho {cmd} >> {log}\nexit 1\n")
            os.chmod(stub, 0o755)
        env = {"PATH": stubdir + os.pathsep + "/usr/bin:/bin",
               "PYTHONSAFEPATH": "1"}
        fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("gen_fixtures.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", _tools_path("verify_offline.sh"), fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()
        # Copies carrying network-word comments behave identically. The
        # copies sit in a mirrored Tools/ layout with Lib linked back to
        # the repo, because the verifier derives its root from its own
        # path; only the trailing comment differs from the real scripts.
        mirror = os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Tools", "packagenamespaces")
        os.makedirs(mirror)
        os.symlink(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "Lib"),
                   os.path.join(tmp, "mirror", "Lib"))
        commented = {}
        for script in ("gen_fixtures.sh", "verify_offline.sh"):
            with open(_tools_path(script), encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                content = handle.read()
            copy_path = os.path.join(mirror, script)
            with open(copy_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                handle.write(content + comment)
            commented[script] = copy_path
        alt_fixtures = os.path.join(tmp, "alt-fixtures")
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["gen_fixtures.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", commented["verify_offline.sh"], alt_fixtures],
            capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/", timeout=300, env=env)
        assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
        assert "verify: all checks passed" in result.stdout
        assert not os.path.exists(log), open(log).read()

__all__ = ['SecurityPolicy']


class SecurityPolicy:
    """Allow projects owned by owner under its active policy namespaces."""

    def __init__(self, namespaces, owner):
        _validate_owner(owner)
        if isinstance(namespaces, str):
            namespaces = (namespaces,)
        try:
            namespaces = iter(namespaces)
        except TypeError:
            raise InvalidNamespaceError(
                'namespaces must be an iterable of names'
            ) from None
        self._namespaces = tuple(_validate_name(name) for name in namespaces)
        self._owner = owner

    @property
    def namespaces(self):
        return self._namespaces

    @property
    def owner(self):
        return self._owner

    def allows(self, project, index):
        """Check project ownership and an active grant on this index."""
        project = normalize_name(project)
        if (not index.supports_namespaces
                or index.project_owner(project) != self.owner):
            return False
        for namespace in self.namespaces:
            grant = index.store.get(namespace)
            if (grant is not None and grant.owner == self.owner
                    and namespace_matches(namespace, project)):
                return True
        return False

    def evaluate(self, requirements, index):
        """Return normalized project names mapped to their policy decisions."""
        return {normalize_name(project): self.allows(project, index)
                for project in requirements}

from .grants import _validate_name, _validate_owner

__all__ = [
    'CONFLICT_STATUS', 'UploadConflictError', 'GrandfatheredRegistry',
    'authorize_upload',
]

CONFLICT_STATUS = 409


class UploadConflictError(Exception):
    """An uploader does not own a matching reserved namespace."""

    status_code = CONFLICT_STATUS

    def __init__(self, project, namespace, owner):
        self.project = normalize_name(project)
        self.namespace = normalize_name(namespace)
        self.owner = owner
        super().__init__(
            f'409 Conflict: {owner!r} cannot upload {self.project!r}; '
            f'namespace {self.namespace!r} is reserved'
        )


class GrandfatheredRegistry:
    """Keep normalized project names exempt from namespace upload checks."""

    def __init__(self, projects=()):
        self._projects = set()
        for project in projects:
            self.add(project)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._projects)

    def __contains__(self, project):
        return (isinstance(project, str)
                and normalize_name(project) in self._projects)

    def add(self, project):
        """Exempt a project from namespace upload checks."""
        self._projects.add(_validate_name(project))

    def discard(self, project):
        """Remove an exemption, if present."""
        self._projects.discard(normalize_name(project))

    def covers(self, project):
        """Return whether the normalized project is exempt."""
        return project in self

    def projects(self):
        """Return exempt project names in sorted order."""
        return sorted(self._projects)


def authorize_upload(project, owner, store, grandfathered=None):
    """Return True when allowed, otherwise raise UploadConflictError.

    Validate the uploader before consulting grants, even for unreserved or
    grandfathered projects.  Exemptions apply to complete project names.
    """
    _validate_owner(owner)
    project = _validate_name(project)
    if grandfathered is not None and grandfathered.covers(project):
        return True
    for grant in store.matching(project):
        if grant.owner != owner:
            raise UploadConflictError(project, grant.name, owner)
    return True

class _AnchorCollector(HTMLParser):
    """Collect anchors as (href, text) with entities resolved.

    Tag and attribute names compare case-insensitively and attribute
    formatting (quote style, spacing around `=`, extra attributes) is
    free: any page a real parser reads the same way passes.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.anchors = []
        self._current = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower() == "a":
            lowered = {name.lower(): value for name, value in attrs}
            self._current = (lowered.get("href"), [])

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self._current is not None:
            self._current[1].append(data)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower() == "a" and self._current is not None:
            href, chunks = self._current
            self.anchors.append((href, "".join(chunks)))
            self._current = None


def _collect_anchors(page):
    collector = _AnchorCollector()
    collector.feed(page)

    need_impl()
    import argparse
    from packagenamespaces import build_parser

    assert callable(build_parser)

    assert isinstance(parser, argparse.ArgumentParser), type(parser)
    parser.parse_args(["reserve", "acme", "--owner", "acme-corp"])

#!/bin/bash
# Control harness: probe the reward signal with known-good/known-bad trees.
#
# Prints RAW REWARDS only -- no verdicts.  The controls gate applies the
# policy itself (pos -> 1, neg -> 0, twice -> identical).
#
#   CONTROL-BEGIN <kind> <name>     before each control runs
#   CONTROL pos <name> reward=<r>   correct but differently written
#   CONTROL neg <name> reward=<r>   wrong / gaming / no-op
#   CONTROL twice <unit> reward=<a>,<b>  same state graded twice
set -uo pipefail

TASKDIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
TASK=ss007-pep752-implicit-namespaces
PLUGIN_ROOT=/home/uldis/cpython/.autopilot/portfolios/accepted-peps-cpython/runtime/62e711dad94714a3c723dc92603cc6cd5599b8859c21abdf532f0b112f43b4d9/lambo-express
IMG=ss007-pep752-controls:v1
STEP=1_pep752
# The task's declared shape (task.toml [environment]); never above 4/8192.
LIMITS="--cpus=4 --memory=8192m --memory-swap=8192m"

"$PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/lh-create-swe-single-turn/scripts/taskbuild.sh" "$TASK" \
    -t "$IMG" -f "$TASKDIR/environment/Dockerfile" "$TASKDIR/environment" \
    >"$TASKDIR/build/.controls-build.log" 2>&1 || {
    echo "run_controls: image build failed; see build/.controls-build.log" >&2
    exit 1
}

stage_and_solve() {
    # $1=cid; stages /tests and /solution, runs solve.sh unless $2 == nosolve.
    local cid="$1" mode="${2:-solve}"
    docker cp "$TASKDIR/steps/$STEP/tests/." "$cid:/tests/" >/dev/null 2>&1
    if [ "$mode" = solve ]; then
        docker exec "$cid" bash -c 'rm -rf /solution && mkdir -p /solution' >/dev/null 2>&1
        docker cp "$TASKDIR/steps/$STEP/solution/." "$cid:/solution/" >/dev/null 2>&1
        docker exec "$cid" bash /solution/solve.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

grade_once() {
    # $1=cid; runs test.sh, prints the reward (0.0 on any failure to read).
    local cid="$1" reward
    docker exec "$cid" bash /tests/test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    reward="$(docker exec "$cid" cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 0.0)"
    if [ "$reward" = "1" ]; then reward="1.0"; fi
    if [ "$reward" = "0" ]; then reward="0.0"; fi
    printf '%s' "$reward"
}

run_control() {
    # $1=kind $2=name $3=mode(nosolve|solve) $4=overlay-dir-or-empty
    local kind="$1" name="$2" mode="$3" overlay="$4" cid reward
    echo "CONTROL-BEGIN $kind $name"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    cid="$(LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name" docker run -d --rm $LIMITS "$IMG" sleep 3600)" || {
        echo "CONTROL $kind $name reward=ERROR_NO_CONTAINER"
        return 0
    }
    export LAMBO_CONTROL="$kind/$name"
    if ! stage_and_solve "$cid" "$mode"; then

class _AnchorCollector(HTMLParser):
    """Collect anchors as (href, text) with entities resolved.

    Tag and attribute names compare case-insensitively and attribute
    formatting (quote style, spacing around `=`, extra attributes) is
    free: any page a real parser reads the same way passes.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.anchors = []
        self._current = None

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag.lower() == "a":
            lowered = {name.lower(): value for name, value in attrs}
            self._current = (lowered.get("href"), [])

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if self._current is not None:
            self._current[1].append(data)

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag.lower() == "a" and self._current is not None:
            href, chunks = self._current
            self.anchors.append((href, "".join(chunks)))
            self._current = None


def _collect_anchors(page):
    collector = _AnchorCollector()
    collector.feed(page)
